name: OCNLI
intro: OCNLI 是不依赖翻译、完全从原生中文材料人工构建的大规模自然语言推理数据集。145 名中文母语的语言相关专业学生基于五种体裁、四种假设生成条件构建语料，并以五标签多数投票复核。论文标题总数为 56,486，但四个子集行相加为 56,525；固定仓库发布为 50,486 条训练、3,000 条验证和 3,000 条隐藏标签测试数据。
org: Indiana University, Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence, CLUE Benchmark
build_method: 原生中文前提采集, 四条件人工假设生成, 五标签复核与多数投票
eval_feature: 原生中文, 四种生成策略, 五标签复核
build_method_en: Native-Chinese Premise Collection, Four-condition Human Hypothesis Elicitation, Five-label Verification and Majority Vote
eval_feature_en: Original Chinese, Four Elicitation Strategies, Five-label Verification
intro_en: OCNLI is a large-scale NLI dataset constructed entirely from original Chinese material without translation. Using five genres and four hypothesis-elicitation conditions, 145 native-Chinese students in language-related majors create the corpus, followed by five-label majority-vote verification. The paper headline total is 56,486, while its four displayed subset rows sum to 56,525; the fixed repository releases 50,486 train, 3,000 validation, and 3,000 test rows with test labels withheld.

drawio_review_note: Paper/source audit fixed on 2026-07-18. The primary paper is arXiv:2010.05444v1; the reviewed PDF has SHA-256 fa195fa1f0657b54441db59a074f53360066cac729a06e37db68f514b65a4b1a. Sections 3-4, Tables 3-4, and Appendices E and G were checked against the diagram. Release rows, label handling, smaller training variants, licensing, and leaderboard behavior were checked at official CLUEbenchmark/OCNLI commit b53efdee17257a5c33993cf6fcf8ffff0497ea0e. OCNLI uses original Chinese rather than translated NLI data. Premises come from government work reports, the news portion of the Lancaster Corpus of Mandarin Chinese, two contemporary novels, TV talk-show transcripts, and Chinese Callhome telephone transcripts. Callhome annotation symbols are removed and source sentences are limited to 8-50 Chinese characters. The 145 hypothesis writers are native Chinese undergraduate or graduate students majoring in Chinese or another language; no one writer is allowed to dominate the corpus. All conditions request entailment, neutral, and contradiction hypotheses and cap hypothesis-premise lexical overlap at 70%. SINGLE follows MNLI with one hypothesis per label and reports 11,986 pairs. MULTI requests up to three per label and reports 12,328; first, second, and third are called easy, medium, and hard solely by elicitation order. MULTI ENCOURAGE reports 16,584 and offers bonuses for diverse hypotheses, including contradictions without negators. MULTI CONSTRAINT reports 15,627 and permits a negator in at most one of the three contradictions, with random checks and reduced payment for violations. A required paper conflict is preserved: those four displayed rows sum to 56,525, but Table 3 and the paper headline report 56,486. The fixed repository's 50,486 training rows after a 6,000-row development/test holdout align with the 56,486 headline, but the public fields do not identify which displayed condition count accounts for the 39-pair discrepancy. Verification is not merely 'about 15 percent': Table 4 gives exact relabel counts of 1,919 SINGLE, 1,994 MULTI, 3,000 ENCOURAGE, and 3,000 CONSTRAINT pairs, corresponding to 16.0%, 16.2%, 18.1%, and 19.2% of the reported subsets. Each receives four independent new labels plus the writer's original label. At least three labels agree on 98.6%, 98.8%, 98.7%, and 98.3% respectively. Majority vote supplies the reference label; no-majority rows are marked '-' and excluded from experiments. The paper randomizes 6,000 relabeled ENCOURAGE/CONSTRAINT pairs into 3,000 validation and 3,000 test examples, balancing the easy/medium/hard elicitation orders; SINGLE, MULTI, and remaining ENCOURAGE/CONSTRAINT data form training. The fixed repository contains 50,486 train rows, 3,000 validation rows, and 3,000 test inputs with labels withheld. It retains 49 '-' rows in train and 50 in validation. The non-overlap train.small release removes premises that also occur in validation/test and contains 30,286 rows; the repository later adds nested 10,000- and 3,000-row samples. Models predict entailment, neutral, or contradiction, exclude '-' references, and report accuracy; paper transformer results average five runs. The conservative human baseline uses 20 explained practice examples followed by 300 random test items. Five uninvolved undergraduates score 90.3%; a separate five-linguistics-PhD group scores 89.3%, and the paper selects the undergraduate result as its unbiased human reference. OCNLI is released under CC BY-NC 2.0, with the LCMC news premises used under ELRA permission. Public test labels remain withheld and the currently reachable CLUE natural-language-inference leaderboard handles test evaluation, so the diagram does not imply local access to hidden references. Formal publication evidence [site-a11x-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 3830×601 (English) and 3805×601 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 3828×599 and 3803×599. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
